messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - serving-runtime error spike on cluster/redwood-prod. symptom tags: cuda-oom, container-restart, node-eviction. triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:01Z

Sam O'Neill: I'm oncall. seeing a surge of OOMKilled + driver resets. anyone seeing the same?

Priya K: yes. `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` followed by `OOMKilled` across multiple pods in inference-runtime. pattern: high memory allocation right after pod startup.

Diego V: autoscaler logs show repeated flapping: rapid scale-up (90 -> 170 GPUs) in ~8m, then aggressive scale-down. Looks like a feedback loop with bursty traffic from a single client.

Marta H: customer logs indicate a large distributed job kicked off around the same time (batch requests from account: data-sim). Could be an internal workload spike.

Juan R: Summary: cold starts -> heavy KV cache rebuild -> high mem allocation -> node memory pressure -> kubelet eviction -> pods reschedule -> repeat. Autoscaler sees CPU/GPU idle after evictions and scales down, then another burst reintroduces pressure.

Sam O'Neill: Immediate mitigation checklist: pause autoscaler scale-down, add scale-step/cooldown, cordon problematic nodes, throttle incoming traffic to heavy-model routes, temporarily lower default KV cache size. I'll coordinate.

Sam O'Neill: `/bin/infractl autoscaler --group=gpu-pool pause-scale-down --reason="incident: prevent thrash"` -> executing now.

deploy-bot: autoscaler pause accepted (operation id=op-1730054339). scale-down suspended for gpu-pool.

Priya K: deploying a runtime flag to cap runtime kv preallocation: `--kv-initial-alloc=64M` for large-model profile. Rolling to 15% first.

Marta H: throttling rule applied at gateway to limit concurrent streams for model-group=large to 50. This should reduce immediate memory pressure.

Diego V: I patched the autoscaler policy: set `scale_up_cooldown=240s`, `scale_down_cooldown=1200s`, `max_scale_step=40` GPUs. This should blunt oscillation.

ops-sre: cordoning nodes with kernel OOM signatures: gpunode-eu-07, gpunode-eu-09. Also increasing kubelet eviction thresholds temporarily: `--eviction-hard=memory.available<200Mi` -> changed to `memory.available<120Mi` for GPU node pool.

Priya K: noticed a subset of crashloops show driver state corruption: `NVRM: os_schedule: schedule timeout` and `nvidia-persistenced` errors. Restarting nvidia-persistenced helped on 2 nodes.

Sam O'Neill: Anyone see evidence that a deployment triggered this? I don't see any recent runtime deploys in the last 2 hours.

deploy-bot: No runtime deploys in the timeframe. Latest runtime changelist was 6h ago.

Alice M: CS reports customers complaining about increased latency and a handful of 503s. I've told them we're mitigating and will follow up with ETA.

Sam O'Neill: Good. Let's also roll a targeted restart of pods on healthy nodes to avoid population of corrupted caches. Deleting pods with `restartPolicy=Always` will cause new pods to come up with the capped KV allocation.

Priya K: Doing that now for model-profile=large: `kubectl delete pods -l profile=large --field-selector=status.phase=Running --grace-period=5` -> rolling 20% at a time.

Diego V: also reducing admission rate for heavy models by adding a temporary admission webhook that rejects new canary rollouts and delays scheduled batch jobs.

Marta H: Found the customer-side burst: they started 200 concurrent streaming sessions due to a scheduled job misconfiguration. CS is reaching out to them to ask for pause.

Alice M: they've acknowledged and agreed to throttle back to 20 concurrent sessions for now.

Sam O'Neill: status: error rates down ~70% since pause and throttles; throughput steadied. Still seeing sporadic OOMs on older nodes.

ops-sre: For nodes with driver issues, we're performing staggered reboots (10 nodes at 3m intervals) to clear stale driver state. Reboots scheduled, set pod disruption budget accordingly.

Priya K: Observed log: `kv-cache: allocating 1.4GiB on startup` -> after cap it's `allocating 64Mi`. New pods coming up are OK.

Diego V: Autoscaler metrics look better: no scale-downs in last 20m, avg GPU util stabilized at 62%.

Sam O'Neill: Decision points for stabilization window: keep scale-down suspended for 45m, keep KV cap in place for 2h, block heavy-model rollouts for 1h, and continue gateway throttle until client's burst is fully drained.

Juan R: I'll follow up with a tuning RFC: add memory-pressure as an autoscaler signal, implement `post-scale stabilization window` (block scale-down X mins after any scale-up), and add `max_concurrent_scale_steps` to prevent large instantaneous changes.

Priya K: engineering follow-ups: implement graceful KV warm-start (allocate incrementally), expose per-model memory limits via policy, add runtime telemetry for preallocation spikes.

ops-sre: infra follow-ups: bump node allocatable memory by ~6% for GPU instance type and add a node-level memory-oom guard to avoid kubelet thrashing. Also add driver watchdog restart policy.

Alice M: Customer comms sent: "We've identified an autoscaling feedback loop amplified by a bursty client workload that caused memory pressure and intermittent errors. We've applied throttles, paused scale-down, and reduced runtime memory preallocation. We'll follow up with a postmortem and remediation plan."

Sam O'Neill: OK, creating incident ticket INC-2026-901 and linking runbook notes. Assigning postmortem lead to Marta H.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-901 created. PagerDuty incident linked.

Sam O'Neill: Handing off to next oncall in 30m. Keep monitors on. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Participants on thread: Sam O'Neill, Priya K, Diego V, Marta H, Juan R, Alice M, incident-bot, ops-sre, deploy-bot
